subject: botany
question_text: Name an alga which shows (a) a haplodiplontic life cycle, (b) a diplontic life cycle.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 4 Plant Kingdom, book p.7, VSAQ 8. The book lists Laminaria and Ectocarpus for haplodiplontic and Fucus for diplontic — consistent with NCERT (Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia and kelps are haplo-diplontic; Fucus is diplontic; Laminaria is a kelp). Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Haplodiplontic — Ectocarpus
steps.why: In a haplodiplontic cycle both a haploid gametophyte and a diploid sporophyte are multicellular, free-living phases. Among algae, Ectocarpus, Polysiphonia and the kelps show this pattern.
common_mistakes: Writing Fucus here — Fucus is the diplontic example.
Writing Spirogyra — Spirogyra is haplontic, the third pattern.
steps.memory_tip: Three cycle words, three algae: haplontic Spirogyra, diplontic Fucus, haplodiplontic Ectocarpus.
steps.margin_note: One correctly paired genus per cycle earns each mark.

steps.label: Diplontic — Fucus
lines: The main plant body is diploid; only the
steps.why: In a diplontic cycle the dominant free-living body is the diploid sporophyte and the haploid stage is only the single-celled gamete — Fucus is the standard algal example.
common_mistakes: Writing a seed plant as the example — seed plants are diplontic, but the question asks for an alga.
Pairing Fucus with haplodiplontic — in Fucus the whole body is diploid.
steps.memory_tip: Learn the pair Fucus–diplontic as one item; it is the only named diplontic alga in the syllabus.
steps.margin_note: The boxed pair alone earns the mark; underline the genus name.

insider_note: One correctly paired example per cycle earns each mark; an unpaired list of algae earns nothing.
